newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Gov says agreement reached on GO bond bill.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Gov says agreement reached on GO bond bill.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar said Thursday that he and legislative leaders reached an agreement on a $659 million general obligation bond bill.
The bill, which Edgar had unsuccessfully tried to get passed by the General Assembly for two years, would funnel bond proceeds to prison, higher education and other projects.
The bill had been opposed in the past by House Democrats.

At a press briefing in his Chicago office after a closed-door meeting with legislative leaders, Edgar said he was able to convince House Speaker Michael Madigan, D-Chicago, that a lot of the projects needed funding on an emergency basis.
The Republican governor added that another factor was Moody's Investors Service Inc's upgrade of the state's GO rating to Aa3 from A1 on Monday.
Edgar said Madigan had expressed concern in the past about the state's ratings, which were downgraded in recent years by Moody's and Standard & Poor's Corp.

The governor said the agreement matches a bond bill passed by the Republican-controlled Senate last week. That bill allows for $500 million of the $659 million of GO bonds to be sold as college savings bonds.
Mike Lawrence, Edgar's spokesman, said the Democrat-controlled House is expected to act on the bill next week.
Edgar also said he will propose new bond-financed capital projects in the fiscal 1998 budget he is scheduled to unveil next month.
